cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to believers living as exiles, scattered across a bunch of regions (1 Pet 1:1). He just told them to repay insults with blessing, not with more insults (1 Pet 3:9). Now he asks them a question: "Who can harm you if you are zealous for what is good?"
What a question. But Peter keeps it REAL: even when you're all in for what's good, you could still suffer for doing what's right.

cards.question: Even if they suffer for doing what's right, Peter says the believers are ___.

cards.text: Then Peter says, "Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken." Friend, I lived in a junk drawer for YEARS, and every time somebody yanked it open looking for tape, I got SHAKEN.

cards.question: Instead of fearing, Peter tells the believers to sanctify Christ as Lord. Where?

cards.text: Next, Peter says to always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks. Always prepared? Baker, I once showed up to my own bakery without my APRON.

cards.question: When someone asks, what does Peter say the believers should be ready to explain?

answers.text: The reason for the hope in them

cards.question: Peter says to answer anyone who asks with gentleness and respect.

cards.text: Gentle. Respectful. Not like the group chat where somebody answers everything in ALL CAPS. And Peter says to keep a clear conscience while they do it.

cards.question: Some people will still slander the believers. What does Peter say their good behavior in Christ will do to those people?

answers.text: Turn the whole town against them

cards.text: Then Peter says suffering may come, if it's God's will. But not all suffering is the same.

cards.question: If suffering comes and it's God's will, Peter says suffering for doing evil is better than suffering for doing good.

cards.text: Now Peter points the believers to the One who went before them. Because Christ ALSO suffered for sins.

cards.question: Peter says Christ suffered for sins. How many times?
Peter says Christ suffered, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God.

cards.text: Then Peter says it plainly: He was put to death in the body. But hold on, baker. Peter's not done with that sentence.

cards.question: After Christ was put to death in the body, Peter says He stayed dead.

cards.text: Stay with me, friend, because this part goes DEEP. Peter says Christ also went and preached to the spirits in prison, spirits who disobeyed long ago.

cards.question: Those spirits disobeyed long ago, while God waited patiently. In whose days?

cards.text: God waited patiently while the ark was being built. Me? I can't wait patiently for ONE batch to cool.

cards.question: In the ark, only ___ souls were saved through water.

cards.text: Then Peter takes the water from Noah's day and links it to something else. Watch this, baker. It's a beautiful connection.

cards.question: Peter says the water of Noah's day symbolizes the ___ that now saves you also.
Peter says baptism is about washing dirt off the body.
If baptism isn't about dirt, what does Peter call it?

answers.text: A pledge of a clear conscience toward God
A promise to keep every law of God
A record of good works before God

cards.text: And it saves through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God. Let that sink in, baker: that's where He IS.

cards.question: Peter says angels, authorities and powers are what to Jesus now?

findings.problem: The setup line 'But hold on, baker. Peter's not done with that sentence.' signals a turn after 'put to death in the body', which rules out the answer True on card 5 ('Peter says He stayed dead') before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The walkthrough never tells the baker that Christ was 'made alive in the Spirit' (1 Peter 3:18). Card 5 only asks whether He stayed dead, and no story card says this. This is also the Spirit 'in whom' He went and preached (3:19), so the baker misses an important detail of the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Noah first appears in the walkthrough as the right answer on card 7. Neither card 7 nor card 8 says simply who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question asks what the believers' good behavior 'will do' to those who slander them. 1 Peter 3:16 states a purpose: 'so that those who slander you may be put to shame'. Saying 'will' makes the text more certain than it is.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: 'Watch this, baker. It's a beautiful connection.' is filler that reads as a nice dad being pleasant. Stop 2 has only one real laugh (card 8), and this card is a natural spot to push the voice further.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
